decision: premise confirmed: no ladder mode on main; all rungs exist as separate flags
why: plan builds a switch and an aim, not new levelling

decision: ladder = option defaults + per-file aim (profile hash, own :lufs), not a new levelling class
why: GainPlan, Compression and the tolerance checks already take a profile; an aim reuses them unchanged (model-the-domain: one shape for where a file is aimed; laziness: no new layer)
evidence: processor.rb process_file_two_pass already runs compression, peak-limited, gain in ladder order

decision: target is two settings: --anchor programme|dialogue and --target-level
why: Will's choices are dialogue -27, dialogue -24 or programme -20 (research 0002 rows F/G), so anchor and level vary independently

decision: programme anchor keeps the existing profile name; recipe 3 marks the method
why: profile = where to aim, recipe = how (recipe.rb); a new name would re-level every done file on a default flip
evidence: skip_decider.rb matches on profile name; Recipe never re-levels without --redo-recipe
result: ladder on a livingroom library re-levels nothing unless --redo-recipe 2

decision: the flip is Recipe::CURRENT = LADDER; --ladder and Processor default to CURRENT == LADDER
why: one source of truth for the default; task asks for a one-line flip
evidence: spec ladder_spec 'is on by default once the default recipe is the ladder'

decision: check_redoable! judges against the recipe the run writes
why: a ladder run must be able to redo recipe 2; a constant-gain run still can't redo its own

decision: dynamic runs (--allow-dynamic, --fast, night) turn the ladder off with a note instead of refusing
why: after the flip those flags must still work alone; dialogue anchor with them is refused because it has no meaning without the ladder

decision: old ffmpeg drops rung 2, --fast-verify drops rung 3, each with a note; explicit flags keep their existing refusals
why: CI runs 4.2 where --limit-db is refused; the default must not break there after the flip

decision: dialogue anchor: no estimate -> programme target+3; loudness above dialogue floored at 0; re-read dialogue through the compression chain
why: Netflix -24 programme for -27 dialogue; a centre louder than the mix is a bad estimate; compression moves programme and dialogue differently

decision: rung derived from stamp (mode, codec change, object profile), not stamped
why: works for files made before the ladder; no new tag needed for it

decision: stamp TARGET_I and DIALOGUE_I only for dialogue-anchored files; LeftRecord target_i
why: report's computed rate must judge a dialogue-anchored file against its own programme target

decision: real-ffmpeg fixtures per rung pass on ffmpeg 7.1.1
why: prove-it-works: run the real CLI and read the output with ebur128, not the deciding filter
evidence: bundle exec rspec spec/ladder_real_spec.rb: 7 examples, 0 failures
